name: Mormyridae
description: Weakly electric fish intelligence with the largest brain-to-body ratio of any fish — comparable to humans. Generates species-specific electric organ discharges (EODs) through modified muscle cells, then reads the distortions of that self-generated field through thousands of electroreceptors distributed across the skin. Simultaneously communicates identity, sex, dominance, and species via pulse waveform shape, and navigates murky water by sensing how objects distort the field. Two sensory pathways process the same signal differently: knollenorgans decode communication (other fish's pulses) while mormyromasts decode electrolocation (self-generated field distortion). This dual-channel architecture — generating a signal and reading its environment-modified return — is the biological equivalent of active radar, and it runs on a brain that processes temporal intervals with microsecond precision.

core_attributes.neurology: cerebellum-dominant massive brain, dual electroreceptor pathways, microsecond temporal resolution
core_attributes.pattern: active electrolocation, species-specific pulse coding, self-generated field analysis

scope.definition: Spatial resolution of mormyrid active electrolocation — minimum distinguishable object separation at 10 cm range, expressed as fraction of body length.

evidence.source: Heiligenberg (1991) 'Neural Nets in Electric Fish', MIT Press; von der Emde (1999) 'Active electrolocation of objects in weakly electric fish', Journal of Experimental Biology 202:1205-1215.
cross_domain_examples: Gnathonemus petersii resolves 2 objects 2.5 mm apart at 10 cm — fine-grain 3D scene reconstruction
active electrolocation provides material property discrimination unavailable to passive systems
bat sonar: convergent active sensing system with analogous resolution-range tradeoff
submarine active sonar: same active-emission-plus-return-analysis architecture at macroscale

scope.falsifiability: If mormyrid object-discrimination performance in controlled tasks is not above chance for objects <5 mm apart, the claimed spatial resolution is overstated.
scope.measurement_limits: Resolution degrades rapidly beyond 10 cm (electric field falls as inverse cube of distance). Conductivity of surrounding water strongly affects signal-to-noise. Resolution is object-material dependent.

scope.definition: Specificity of mormyrid species and individual recognition from electric organ discharge (EOD) waveform alone, measured as classification accuracy of trained conspecifics in playback experiments.

evidence.source: Hopkins (1988) 'Social communication in the aquatic environment', in Sensory Biology of Aquatic Animals; Terleph & Moller (2003) EOD communication specificity.
cross_domain_examples: mormyrids recognize individual conspecific EOD waveforms with 0.91 accuracy in habituation tests
EOD waveform encodes species, sex, and individual identity in nested spectral features
electric eel discharge: high-voltage version of same organ system — species-specific spectral signatures

scope.falsifiability: If mormyrids fail to discriminate own-species from heterospecific EOD in controlled playback, species-level recognition via EOD is not supported.
scope.measurement_limits: Communication function is active only when background electrical noise is below EOD amplitude. Mormyrids in groups produce pulse interference that degrades individual recognition at close range.

scope.definition: Independence of mormyrid electrosensory and mechanosensory (lateral line) processing — proportion of object-detection tasks solvable by electrosensory pathway alone, measured by selective pathway ablation.

evidence.source: Bodznick & Boord (1986) mormyrid electrosensory processing; Engelmann et al. (2002) electrosensory vs mechanosensory task separation.
cross_domain_examples: lateral line ablation: mormyrids retain 0.90 of normal object discrimination using electrosense alone
electrosense ablation: 0.35 performance retention on same tasks via lateral line — weaker channel
human visual and auditory cortices: similarly independent parallel processing channels for object recognition

scope.falsifiability: If electrosensory ablation reduces discrimination performance to chance, the dual-channel architecture provides no redundancy — electrosense is the single functional channel.
scope.measurement_limits: Channel independence is task-dependent: far-field objects (>20 cm) rely on electrosense; turbulent flow detection relies on lateral line. Integration occurs in midbrain for complex scenes.

scope.definition: Temporal precision of mormyrid EOD pulse timing — jitter (standard deviation of inter-pulse interval) as fraction of mean interval, reflecting precision of neural oscillator controlling discharge.

evidence.source: Moller (1995) 'Electric Fishes: History and Behavior', Chapman & Hall; Brienomyrus brachyistius timing studies in Bell (2001).
cross_domain_examples: mormyrid pulse timing jitter <10 microseconds (CV <0.001) — precision exceeding most neural oscillators
pulse timing disruption in conspecific interaction is detected within 20 µs — social signal resolution
atomic clock precision analogue: biological oscillator achieving sub-millisecond temporal stability

scope.falsifiability: If mormyrid EOD timing jitter is measured above 100 µs in controlled electrophysiology, the microsecond-precision oscillator model is incorrect.
scope.measurement_limits: Timing precision degrades with water temperature (enzyme kinetics slow below 20°C) and during social interactions when pulse patterns are modified for communication.
